Mass analyzers are devices used in mass spectrometry to separate ions based on their mass-to-charge ratios. The resolution of a mass analyzer refers to its ability to distinguish between ions with similar mass-to-charge ratios.

Among the four options provided:

A. Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance (FT-ICR)
B. Orbitrap
C. Quadrupole 
D. Time-of-flight (TOF)

FT-ICR mass analyzers generally have the highest resolving power, capable of reaching resolutions exceeding 1,000,000. They operate by measuring the cyclotron frequency of ions in a strong magnetic field, which can be determined with extremely high precision.

Orbitraps also have excellent resolution (typically up to 150,000-240,000), but not as high as FT-ICR.

Quadrupoles have relatively low resolution (typically around 2,000-5,000).

Time-of-flight analyzers have moderate resolution (typically up to 40,000-60,000 with reflectron designs).

Therefore, in terms of resolution, Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance (FT-ICR) mass analyzers are the best among the given options.

Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
